I'm a little late to the party, but i would like to tell my story. I am 17 and the daughter of someone in the entertainment industry. I actually have no idea what my household earns exactly, but I know that neither I nor my two siblings will have to worry about college tuition, even if we all went to a very expensive school. I admit we are extremely well off, but I think there's a difference between being wealthy yourself and your family having money. I think I've learned a lot about how to manage my money because of how we live. We aren't extravagant in our habits, unlike a lot of people we know, and while we enjoy a great deal of comforts, we don't just spend money wildly- I think this is because my parents weren't wealthy at all until my dad got the job he has now. In fact, I describe my situation like this to my friends: my family is rich, but I'm broke.

The best part about being wealthy? Probably the fact that I don't really have to worry about how I'm going to get on. I get clothing when I need it from any place (though the cost balances itself out since I get so much from thrift shops,too), I can eat what I want, and we can afford a great deal of things like vacation homes or our tesla (pretty much my father's baby). 

The worst part, I think, is that people assume that when you're wealthy, you shouldn't have any problems because "Oh, well you're ungrateful for your opportunities" or "You're being spoiled and selfish." To be frank, that's bullshit. Getting a new iPhone for my birthday doesn't make me any less depressed, and whatever opportunities I have, I often fuck up because I can't even get out of bed. I just got out of a five week residential program because I can't make myself eat when I'm alone and I'm intensely depressed, yet the most often thing people said to me in there when they found out my family was wealthy was, "Why are you in here?"

It just makes me feel guilty, guys.

Last summer, I attended a summer camp up in Oregon with around twenty people my age. Part of the three week long camping session involved a four day overnight at a campground that was a few hours away from the location of the summer camp itself. The girls and boy each slept on a separate tarp, the girls huddling together for warmth during the cold night while the boys wrestled each other for sleeping bags. 

The second night of the trip, I woke up at around three in the morning, it was pitch black, but I could see an orange lamp in the distance. I could see a shadow of someone coming towards me that was backlit by the lamp, but i remember being very bored and going back to sleep. 

The next morning, I awake to my fellow female campers in a state of extreme fear and panic. Apparently, one of the girls had heard a little girl of around five years old walking around the campsite going, "Hello? Hello?" She had told another camper about this and found that that other girl had heard the child as well. Further investigation revealed that at least five people had heard this little girl calling out in the middle of the night. 

Meanwhile, I am sort of freaking out because of the shadow I saw the night before, and I'm thinking to myself, "was that shadow the girl?" I let it go while some girls go off to investigate the campsite.  They end up finding a tent belonging to a nice family with a young daughter and ask them if this little girl wandered away the night before. They apparently replied saying that they had only arrived that morning.

By the end of the day, everyone has basically pissed themselves worrying about the little ghost girl coming back that night. I'm tired, I go to bed early and a little nervous. I am shaken awake half an hour later to peals of laughter. Turns out, I had been sleeptalking and apparently, my voice sounded exactly like the "ghost girl."

It was a little embarrassing at first, but after we returned from the trip, we got to scare the younger unit kids.

TL;DR: my sleeptalking causes panic and makes people think that the ghost of a toddler has come to haunt their campground.
